LESSON: WRITING 11.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.4: Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing, part of Strand 11 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words? 2. Which are some of the words with same or opposite meaning?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen/watch a video recording on in-door games and identify words with synonyms and antonyms,

2. form sentences using synonyms and antonyms,

3. identify synonyms and antonyms from newspapers, magazines or the internet and create a crossword puzzle,

4. display their work on posters. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen/watch a video recording on in-door games and identify words with synonyms and antonyms,
2. form sentences using synonyms and antonyms,
3. identify synonyms and antonyms from newspapers, magazines or the internet and create a crossword puzzle,
4. display their work on posters. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 11.4.1 Mechanics of writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to Learn: The learner’s ability to learn on their own is enhanced as they engage in self-driven tasks such as

identifying synonyms and antonyms from newspapers, magazines or the internet.
